aiRule: Attempt problems yourself first. Use AI only as reviewer/mentor after your attempt. The one exception is the code-comprehension drills, where using an assistant and then verifying its output is the skill being practised.
goal: Google SWE interview readiness (L3/early L4) while becoming a stronger independent engineer.
targetLevelNote: The plan is built for L3/L4, where 3–4 coding rounds plus one Googleyness & Leadership round decide the loop. System design is studied for engineering judgement and for the optional L4 design round — it is not the deciding signal at this level.

skillTargets.target: All 164 curated problems solved once by week 20, then revisited under time; mediums under ~35 minutes
Production-quality idioms for backend coding rounds and take-home clarity; all 50 Go bank items covered in teaching order, basics through code comprehension
Explain OS, DBMS, and OOP trade-offs without slides in under 8 minutes; all 35 items covered
Trace a request path and justify timeout, retry, and auth choices; all 25 items covered
Complete one HLD and one LLD mock per month with explicit trade-offs; all 30 items covered
Think-aloud coding, STAR-L behavioral stories, and Googleyness examples — each of the 33 items rehearsed to delivery standard

phases.title: Foundations
phases.focus: Arrays, hashing, two pointers, sliding window and prefix sums; Go language core; OS refresher; daily think-aloud habit
outcomes: Solve array/hash and two-pointer mediums without pattern hints
Write idiomatic Go with table tests for small utilities
Explain process vs thread and virtual memory in plain language
Complete the first four Saturday retention assessments

phases.title: Structures
phases.focus: Stack, linked list, binary search and binary search on answer; Go errors, interfaces and testing; DBMS indexes and ACID; DNS and TCP
outcomes: Pick the right monotonic-stack or two-pointer variant on sight
Write binary search with no off-by-one and justify the invariant
Explain an index choice and an isolation level to a non-specialist
Trace a browser request from DNS through TCP

phases.title: Trees and graphs
phases.focus: Tree DFS/BFS, trie, graph traversal, topological sort, union-find and Dijkstra; Go concurrency; TLS and load balancing; design method
outcomes: BFS/DFS and topological sort under time pressure
Build a handler chain with context cancellation in Go
Diagram the DNS-to-TLS path for a browser request
Draft a URL shortener HLD with back-of-envelope numbers

phases.title: Advanced algorithms
phases.focus: 1-D and 2-D DP, knapsack, LIS, backtracking; production Go (net/http, database/sql, observability); storage, caching and queues
outcomes: Recognise DP state transitions on common Google variants
Implement SQL transactions and explain isolation anomalies
Design a rate limiter and a notification system with failure modes
Ship a small Go service with tests, middleware and structured logs

phases.title: Interview strength
phases.focus: Greedy, bit manipulation and the remaining patterns; full HLD and LLD walk-throughs; STAR-L bank; code-comprehension drills
outcomes: Two Pramp or interviewing.io sessions with a written retro
Five polished STAR-L stories mapped to Googleyness attributes
Read and debug an unfamiliar 300-line codebase aloud in 45 minutes
Complete a full HLD and a full LLD without notes

phases.title: Integration
phases.focus: Mixed timed sets, spaced revision across every pattern, weak-area sprints, remaining design and reliability topics
outcomes: Weekly Saturday mock covering coding plus one design prompt
Every pattern revisited at least twice under time
Bottom-quartile DSA tags brought back to green
Behavioural bank delivered from memory, not from notes

phases.title: Polish
phases.focus: Full-loop simulations, resume narrative, rest and confidence calibration
outcomes: Two full-day onsite simulations (coding, design, behavioural)
One-page system design cheat sheet written from memory
Question list for interviewers and thank-you templates ready
Light review only — no new heavy topics in the final 72 hours before real loops

weeklyRhythm.weekday: Sunday–Friday, 120 min exactly: communication speak (15) + DSA practice (65) + skill learn (40). On Thursday the skill block becomes a spaced DSA review instead. No timed assessments on study days.
weeklyRhythm.weekend: Saturday only, 240 min: weekly mock (90) + retention assessment (30) + timed DSA set with retro (120). No regular study backlog is scheduled on Saturday.
weeklyRhythm.assessment: All tests, assessments, and mocks are Saturday-only. Sunday–Friday are study days. You may complete any future day's tasks ahead.

dsaCoverage.rule: Every problem is introduced exactly once in weeks 1–20 in pattern order, then revisited in spaced review slots, Saturday timed sets, and the weeks 21–26 revision blocks. No problem is introduced twice.
